title: Card Deck
story: A deck of cards is a perfect data structure: 52 unique items with suits and ranks, needing to be created, shuffled, and dealt. Cards appear in poker, blackjack, solitaire, and magic tricks. Build the fundamental card operations that power every card game.
why: Building a card deck teaches enums for suits/ranks, Vec for the deck, Fisher-Yates shuffle, and dealing — all composable into any card game.
analogy: A physical deck of cards: 52 unique rectangles, shuffled by splitting and riffling. Your Vec[Card] is the box, Fisher-Yates shuffle is the riffle, dealing pops cards off the top like dealing from a real deck. The abstraction is so clean it feels like holding actual cards.
try_it: Expand to full 52-card deck with all 4 suits and 13 ranks. Add a `card_name(c: &Card) -> Str` function that returns 'Ace of Spades', 'King of Hearts', etc. Shuffle the deck and deal 5 cards (a poker hand). Print the hand.
tips: Fisher-Yates shuffle: iterate backwards, swap with random position ≤ current index
Deal from the end of the Vec — no shifting needed after removal
4 suits × 13 ranks = 52 cards — iteration over enums builds the deck
common_mistakes: Shuffling by swapping random positions without the ≤ i constraint — Fisher-Yates is uniform only when j ≤ i
Dealing from the front — removal from front shifts all elements (O(n))
Not cloning cards before removing — ownership rules require a copy
